title: About
text:
The Open Handbook Commons is a community project that creates practical books about everyday life skills. Our goal is to make useful knowledge available to everyone, no matter where they live or what their background is.
The books cover simple and practical topics that help people in daily life. These include skills such as cooking, sewing and mending, home repair, basic survival, outdoor skills, digital literacy, and other useful knowledge. All books are written in simplified English so they are easier to read and understand, including for people who are not native English speakers.
Our books are released as downloadable, print-ready PDF files. Anyone can read them on a computer or phone, or print them and share them with others.
Every book published by this project is released under the Creative Commons Attribution–NonCommercial–ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) license. This means you are free to download, print, share, and adapt the material for personal and educational use. You must give proper credit, and any modified versions must use the same license. Commercial printing or selling the books is not allowed without permission.
All repositories in this organization are also licensed under CC BY-NC-SA unless a repository states otherwise.

Disclaimers
The information in these books is provided for education, learning, and hobby use only and is shared “as is.” We do not guarantee that all information is complete or suitable for every situation. The Open Handbook Commons and its contributors are not responsible for any problems, damages, or losses that may result from using this information. Readers are responsible for making sure that any use of the information is safe and lawful.
Some content may be written or edited with the help of AI tools, especially to convert text into simplified English - all content is reviewed by human contributors.
The community works to avoid plagiarism and to respect the work of others. If you find content that may be copied without proper credit or permission, please report it to contact@openhandbook.org, and we will review it.

title: Digital Literacy
text:
Digital technology is now part of everyday life. Many people use computers, smartphones, and the internet every day. We use these tools to communicate with others, learn new things, work, read news, watch videos, and store information.
Because of this, it is important to understand how to use digital technology in a safe, responsible, and effective way. This ability is called digital literacy.
Digital literacy is more than knowing how to use a computer or a phone. It also includes knowing how to find reliable information on the internet, communicate respectfully online, protect personal information, recognize scams and false information, and create and share digital content responsibly.
This book is written to help readers learn these skills. It explains digital tools and ideas in clear and simple language. The chapters introduce common technologies, explain how the internet works, and discuss topics such as online safety, misinformation, and responsible online behavior.
This book is written for students, teachers, self-learners, and anyone who wants to better understand the digital world. No advanced technical knowledge is required to read this book.
Technology continues to change quickly. New tools and services appear every year. The goal of digital literacy is not only to learn how to use current tools, but also to develop the skills needed to learn and adapt in the future.
We hope this book helps readers feel more confident when using digital technology and encourages thoughtful and responsible use of the internet and digital tools.

title: Contribute
text:
This project depends on community contributions. People can help in many ways. Some contributions are technical, such as writing new sections, editing chapters, or helping improve the tools used to build and publish the books and this website. Other contributions are simpler but equally valuable, such as correcting typos and grammar, checking facts, identifying possible plagiarism, suggesting improvements, or helping make the text clearer.
We track suggestions and changes mainly through GitHub, where contributors can open issues, submit pull requests, or start discussions.
If you are not familiar with GitHub, you can still contribute. Simply send your suggestions or corrections by email to contact@openhandbook.org. We will review them and include them in the project when appropriate.

title: Contribute
text:
Author Guidelines

Writing Style
Authors contributing to Open Handbook Commons are encouraged to write in simplified English. Simplified English means writing in a clear and easy way so that many readers can understand the text. Many readers of open books are not native English speakers, so simple language helps make the material more accessible.
Try to use common words and short sentences. Avoid slang, idioms, and unnecessarily complex vocabulary. If a technical term is required, briefly explain it the first time it appears.
Organize your writing so it is easy to read. Use short paragraphs, clear headings, and lists or numbered steps when explaining procedures. Write in a direct and practical style. The goal is not to sound academic or complicated. The goal is to help readers understand the information quickly and clearly.


AI Usage
You may use AI or LLM tools to help edit your writing, check grammar, or convert text into simplified English (recommended). However, contributors remain responsible for reviewing the content before submission. Make sure the information is accurate and that the writing reflects your own work.
AI tools should assist with clarity and editing, but they should not replace careful human review.


Plagiarism
Open Handbook Commons respects the work of others and expects contributors to avoid plagiarism. Plagiarism means copying text, ideas, images, or other content from someone else without proper credit. Contributions should generally be written in your own words.
If you use information from books, articles, websites, or other sources, clearly cite or link to the original source. Short quotations may be used when necessary, but they should be clearly marked and credited.
To avoid plagiarism, read the source material first and then explain the idea in your own words instead of copying sentences. When including facts, data, or specific ideas from another work, provide a reference so readers know where the information came from.
Authors are encouraged to review their work before submission and ensure that the text is original. Several free tools can help check for possible plagiarism, including Quetex, SmallSEOTools Plagiarism Checker, Duplichecker, and Grammarly’s plagiarism checker. These tools can help identify sections of text that may closely match other published content.


Self-Contained Writing
Because our books are intended to be downloaded and printed, we encourage authors to write in a self-contained way whenever possible. Important information should be included directly in the book rather than relying heavily on external websites.
Links on the internet can change or disappear over time. When this happens, readers may not be able to verify information or follow references. For this reason, authors should try to explain concepts clearly within the text and include key details, examples, or summaries instead of relying only on external links.
External links can still be used when necessary, but they should support the content rather than replace it. The more complete and self-contained a chapter or article is, the more useful and reliable the book will remain for future readers. When adding a link, consider whether it is likely to still exist many years from now.

title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
text:
What is Open Handbook Commons?
Open Handbook Commons is a community project that creates practical books about everyday life skills. These books are designed to be simple, useful, and accessible to anyone, regardless of background or location.


What kind of topics do the books cover?
The books focus primarily on practical skills that people can use in daily life. Topics include cooking, sewing and mending, home repair, outdoor skills, basic survival, digital literacy, and other useful areas. However, broader academic or trade-related topics are also welcome.


Who are these books for?
The books are for everyone. They are especially helpful for:

People who want to learn practical skills
Beginners with little or no prior knowledge
Readers who prefer clear and simple explanations
Non-native English speakers



Why are the books written in simplified English?
We use simplified English to make the content easier to understand for more people. Many readers are not native English speakers, and complex language can make learning harder.
Our goal is clarity, not complexity. Short sentences, common words, and clear explanations help readers learn faster.


How can I read the books?
All books are available as downloadable, print-ready PDF files. You can:

Read them on a computer, tablet, or phone
Print them at home or locally
Share them with others



Can I share or print the books?
Yes. All books are released under the Creative Commons Attribution–NonCommercial–ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) license.
This means you can:

Download and share the books
Print copies for personal or educational use
Adapt the content for non-commercial purposes

You must give proper credit and use the same license for any modified versions. Commercial use is not allowed without permission.


Can I contribute to the project?
Yes. This project depends on community contributions.
You can contribute in many ways:

Writing new content
Editing or improving existing chapters
Fixing grammar or typos
Checking facts
Reporting possible plagiarism
Suggesting improvements



Do I need to know GitHub to contribute?
No. While we mainly use GitHub for contributions, it is not required.
If you are not familiar with GitHub, you can simply email your suggestions or corrections to contact@openhandbook.org, and we will review them.


Why do you allow the use of AI?
We allow the use of AI tools because they help make the project more inclusive.
Many people have valuable knowledge and real-world experience but may find it difficult to write clearly for a general audience. AI tools can help:

Improve grammar
Simplify language
Make writing clearer and more structured

This allows more people to contribute, even if they are not confident writers.
However, AI is only a tool. Contributors are responsible for reviewing their work to ensure accuracy and quality. Human review is always required.


Is AI-generated content allowed without review?
No. All content must be reviewed by human contributors.
AI can assist with writing and editing, but it should not replace careful thinking, fact-checking, and responsibility for the content.


How do you handle plagiarism?
We take plagiarism seriously and check all new submissions using online tools to ensure the content is original.
Contributors are expected to:

Write in their own words
Give proper credit when using other sources
Avoid copying text without permission

If you find content that may be copied without proper credit, please report it to contact@openhandbook.org.


Are the books guaranteed to be accurate?
No. The content is provided for education and learning purposes only and is shared “as is.”
While contributors try to ensure accuracy, we do not guarantee that all information is complete or suitable for every situation. Readers are responsible for using the information safely and appropriately.


Can I use the content for commercial purposes?
No. The license does not allow commercial use without permission.
If you want to use the material commercially (for example, selling printed copies), you must request permission.


How are the books preserved for the long term?
We use long-term archiving through Zenodo to preserve each book.
Zenodo assigns a permanent DOI (Digital Object Identifier) to every release. This means:

Each version of a book is permanently stored
The files remain accessible even if the original repository changes
Readers and researchers can reliably cite the books

GitHub is used for active development and updates, while Zenodo ensures stable, long-term access and preservation.


Where can I find the source code and books?

GitHub organization: https://github.com/openhandbookcommons
Library page: see the full list of books and their repositories



Why are the books designed to be self-contained?
We want the books to remain useful over time, even when printed.
Web links can break or disappear. By keeping content self-contained, readers can understand the material without needing to rely on external websites.


Can I suggest a new book or topic?
Yes. Suggestions are welcome.
You can:

Open an issue on GitHub
Start a discussion
Send an email with your idea



How can I contact the project?

Email: contact@openhandbook.org
